name: Anam
overview: Anam is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as the son of Mizraim. Beyond this genealogical detail, no additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are recorded about him. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Anam appears as a proper name in Scripture without any given meaning or divine origin noted. It is simply recorded as the name of this individual in Genesis 10:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Anam as the son of Mizraim. No other family relationships or descendants are documented beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Anam's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record tracing the descendants of Mizraim, who is traditionally associated with Egypt. This lineage helps establish the biblical framework of nations and peoples following the Flood, underscoring God's sovereign ordering of human history. Although Anam himself is not the focus of specific narratives, his mention contributes to the broader biblical account of humanity's dispersion and God's providential plan.
